newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Three cosmonauts land safely after leaving Mir.
newsitem.headline: Three cosmonauts land safely after leaving Mir.

text.p: Three cosmonauts returning from Russia's Mir space station landed safely in Kazakhstan on Sunday, Interfax news agency said.
The Russian Soyuz TM-24 spacecraft bearing Russians Valery Korzun and Alexander Kaleri and Germany's Reinhold Ewald landed to the east of the Kazakh town of Dzhezkasgan at 0644 GMT, it said.
Mission control near Moscow confirmed the safe landing. Itar-Tass news agency said the cosmonauts "felt well" after their mission and would be flown to Moscow later on Sunday.
The two Russians blasted off into space last August where they conducted more than 200 experiments in new scientific modules under programmes sponsored by the United States, France and Russia.
Ewald spent 20 days in Mir, carrying out medical and technical research.
Russians Vasily Tsibliyev and Alexander Lazutkin and American John Linenger remain on the Mir station to continue medical and biological research.
